instrument_name: 21 V.S.A. 384 Employment; wages (minimum wage; overtime)
authority: Vermont General Assembly (Vermont Statutes Online; Wayback copy 2026-10-24)
figure_or_rule_carried: 384(a)(1): from 2022-01-01 12.55 USD, raised each 1 January by the smaller of 5 percent or CPI-U US city average (12 months preceding the previous 1 September, rounded to one decimal), never decreased, rounded to nearest 0.01. (a)(2): hotel/motel/tourist place/restaurant service or tipped employee (more than 120 USD/month tips) basic wage at least one-half the minimum. (a)(3): federal rate if higher. (b): 1.5x regular rate over 40 h/workweek; exempt: retail or service establishments, seasonal amusement, hotel/motel/restaurant, hospitals etc. electing 8/80 biweekly, transport not under FLSA OT, political subdivisions, FLSA-covered State employees, General Assembly staff. (c): deductions for board, lodging, apparel, rent, utilities. Text includes 2026 session (last amendment 2025 No. 91 eff. 2026-04-30).

instrument_name: 21 V.S.A. 342 Weekly payment of wages (pay frequency, final pay, direct deposit, payroll card) re-read
figure_or_rule_carried: 342(a): weekly pay to a day not more than 6 days before payday; biweekly or semimonthly after notice; CBA may allow 13-day lag. 342(b): voluntary quit paid on the last regular payday (or following Friday if none); discharge paid within 72 hours; absent on payday paid on demand. 342(c): direct deposit or payroll card only with written authorisation; payroll card: plain-language disclosures 10-point type, voluntary written consent not a condition of hire, 3 free withdrawals per period, no employer cost passed on, 21 days notice of changes, 1 free replacement/year, nonbranded card max 60 days, no credit link, free monthly 60-day history on request.

figure_or_rule_carried: Benefit ratio on 3 preceding calendar years; employers ranked into rate classes 0-20 by cumulative payroll; schedule I-V chosen by fund ratio / highest benefit cost rate (quotient 2.50+ = I ... under 1.00 = V); class 0: 0.4/0.6/0.8/1.1/1.3 pct; class 20: 5.4/5.9/6.5/7.7/8.4 pct; 1326(f): rates effective 1 July each year (rate year July-June). instrument_name: 21 V.S.A. 1314a Quarterly wage reporting; misclassification; penalties
figure_or_rule_carried: Quarterly detailed wage report per worker: name, SSN, gross wages in the quarter, plus for hourly workers gender and hourly wage; due by the last day of the month following the quarter; separation information within 10 days of a Commissioner request; penalty 100 USD per late report; misclassification up to 5,000 USD per employee plus up to 3 years State-contract debarment.

instrument_name: 21 V.S.A. 482 Earned sick time (accrual)
figure_or_rule_carried: Accrual at least 1 hour per 52 hours worked; waiting period up to 1 year for new hires (accrues, cannot use); employer may cap accrual at 40 hours per 12 months and at 40 h/week of accrual for FLSA-exempt full-timers; paid at the greater of the normal hourly rate or the 384 minimum wage; group insurance continues; accrual computed each pay period or quarterly.

instrument_name: Vermont DOL Employer Handbook (06/26) re-read: coverage, exempt employment, records, new-employer rate, quarterly due dates, multistate tests, new hire
figure_or_rule_carried: Coverage: domestic service cash wages 1,000+ in a quarter; agricultural 20,000+ in a quarter or 10+ workers. Exempt employment list: elected officials, some nonprofit/religious services, casual labour <=50 USD (non-corporate), commission-only insurance agents and licensed salesmen, J-1 visa holders with documentation, sole proprietor/partner family (child under 18), multi-member LLC members unless IRS election, railroad, foreign vessels, student work-experience, students at their own school, some summer-camp students. Records kept 4 years (per pay period and per worker items listed, incl. in-kind value and reported tips). New employer rate 1 percent for most employers BEGINNING 2004-07-01 (foreign construction NAICS 236/237/238: industry average); new-employer rate for at least two years. Quarterly Wage and Contribution report every quarter even with no wages, electronic via Employer e-Services, due Apr 30 / Jul 31 / Oct 31 / Jan 31, next business day if weekend/holiday; excess wages computed by the system. Multistate: four tests (localization, base of operations, ...). New hire: report within 10 days of first day of work for compensation; rehire after 60+ consecutive days separated is a new hire; name, address, SSN, start date via Employer e-Services; data go to the State Directory of New Hires (Office of Child Support).

instrument_name: 21 V.S.A. 1321(b)(2) wages for other-state employment count toward the Vermont base
figure_or_rule_carried: For the base of contributions: (1) an acquiring employer is treated as a single unit with its predecessor for the calendar year of acquisition; (2) employment includes service constituting employment under any unemployment compensation law of another state, so wages already paid by the same employer for employment covered in another state count toward the Vermont taxable wage base in the same calendar year (MULTI hand-off answered).

instrument_name: 21 V.S.A. 481 Earned sick time definitions (covered employee)
figure_or_rule_carried: Employee = employed an average of at least 18 h/week during a year. Excluded: federal employees; jobs of 20 weeks or fewer in 12 months AND scheduled 20 weeks or fewer; exempt/excluded State classified service; per-diem/intermittent health-care facility staff; non-regular substitute educators; under 18 years of age; sole proprietors/partners and approved excluded executive officers/LLC members (WC exclusions 601(14)(F),(H)); per-diem/intermittent workers who work only when available with no obligation or expectation of continuing employment. Employer = any employer doing business or operating in the State (no headcount floor in this section).

instrument_name: 21 V.S.A. 483 Use of earned sick time (use cap; carry-over; no payout)
figure_or_rule_carried: Uses: own illness/care, family care, domestic violence services, closure of school/business. Increments: smallest the payroll system uses, not below 1 hour required. Use cap: employer may limit use to 40 h per 12 months. Unused time carries over (unless paid out at period end at the employer's discretion, which then does not carry over). No payment of unused earned sick time on separation unless the employer agrees. Rehire within 12 months after discharge: no new waiting period (prior balance not retained unless agreed). Hour-trading in the same pay period allowed.

instrument_name: 21 V.S.A. 383 Definitions (minimum-wage/overtime coverage)
figure_or_rule_carried: Employee for 384 excludes: agriculture; domestic service in or about a private home; US government employees; publicly supported nonprofit activities (except laundry, nurses aides, practical nurses); bona fide executive/administrative/professional; home delivery of newspapers/advertising; taxi-cab drivers; outside salespersons; students working during the school year or regular vacations; elected and appointed municipal officers. Employer = any person employing two or more employees. Last amendment 2025 No. 177 (Adj. Sess.) s. 8d eff. 2026-06-18 (content of that amendment not compared; text read is the current one).

instrument_name: 33 V.S.A. 4110 Employer obligations (medical support; new-hire reporting)
figure_or_rule_carried: (a) medical support order: enrol the child regardless of enrolment season, withhold the employee premium share, notify the insurer within 10 days of the 15 V.S.A. 663(d) notice. (b) New hires reported to the Department of Labor within 10 calendar days of first date of employment: employee name, address, first date of employment, SSN; employer name, address, FEIN; electronically when practicable; collusion penalty up to 500 USD. (c) employee/employer per IRC ch. 24 / 3401(d) incl. government and labour organisations; new hire = never employed or separated 60+ consecutive days.

instrument_name: 9 V.S.A. 2440 Social Security Number Protection Act
figure_or_rule_carried: A business may not: make an SSN available to the general public; print it on an access card; require Internet transmission unless secure/encrypted; print an SSN on materials mailed to the individual unless State or federal law requires it on the document (and never visible on a postcard or unopened envelope); disclose to a third party lacking a legitimate purpose without written consent. Exceptions: administrative/internal verification, government entities, required by law, redacted SSN. No pay-statement truncation rule as such: a mailed pay statement may not carry the full SSN (no law requires it there); a redacted SSN is outside the prohibition.

instrument_name: GB-1210-2026 percentage-method tables, allowance values and worked example (oracle)
figure_or_rule_carried: Effective 2026-01-01, expires 2026-12-31. Wages subject to VT withholding = wages subject to federal withholding paid to a VT resident or to a nonresident for services in VT. Method: subtract allowances (W-4VT), apply the percentage table. One allowance: annual 5,400.00; weekly 103.85; biweekly 207.69; semimonthly 225.00; monthly 450.00; quarterly 1,350.00; daily 20.77. Annual Single: 0-3,925 nil; 3,925-54,675 3.35%; 54,675-126,775 1,700.13 + 6.60%; 126,775-260,225 6,458.73 + 7.60%; over 260,225 16,600.93 + 8.75%. Annual Married: 0-11,775 nil; 11,775-96,475 3.35%; 96,475-216,525 2,837.45 + 6.60%; 216,525-323,825 10,760.75 + 7.60%; over 323,825 18,915.55 + 8.75%. Weekly Married: 226-1,855 3.35%. Federal W-4 fallback: extra federal withholding on line 6 -> VT extra = 30 pct of it. Non-periodic (supplemental) payments: VT withholding may be estimated at 30 pct of federal withholding. NQDC: 6 pct. Civil-union partners: Married table. WORKED EXAMPLE (oracle): weekly 1,800, Married, 2 allowances: 1,800 - 207.70 = 1,592.30; (1,592.30 - 226) x 0.0335 = 45.77. Reproduced in Python: 45.7711 -> 45.77; annual 6.60 pct bracket constant (54,675-3,925) x 0.0335 = 1,700.125 -> 1,700.13 (round half up); 5,400/52 = 103.846 -> 103.85.

instrument_name: GB-1210-2026 reporting: registration, W-2/1099 filing, WHT-434, Child Care Contribution scope
figure_or_rule_carried: Register for a withholding account via myVTax or Form BR-400; filing frequency set by the Department from annual withholding totals; returns and payments via myVTax or paper. WHT-434 Annual Withholding Reconciliation due January 31, transmittal for W-2/1099; electronic filing required for 10 or more W-2/1099 forms; payroll filing services must file electronically; Vermont no longer participates in the Combined Fed/State program (file W-2/1099 directly with the Department). CCC 0.44 pct on all IRC 3401 wages subject to VT withholding (incl. remote work physically in VT), paid with the same frequency as withholding; not due on courtesy withholding by an out-of-state employer for work outside VT.

instrument_name: 32 V.S.A. 5822 Tax on income of individuals (rates; indexation; 3 pct minimum tax)
figure_or_rule_carried: Rates 3.35 / 6.6 / 7.6 / 8.75 pct; statutory base brackets (unmarried 38,700 / 93,700 / 195,450; joint 64,600 / 156,150 / 237,950); 5822(a)(6): if federal AGI exceeds 150,000, tax is the greater of the table tax or 3 pct of federal AGI (assessment level, not in withholding tables). 5822(b)(2): brackets indexed annually by the Commissioner of Taxes using the CPI-U adjustment in the federal manner. Assessment-level; withholding uses the GB-1210 tables (US-VTS5-016).

instrument_name: 21 V.S.A. 341 Definitions (wage payment subchapter: ABC test; wages)
figure_or_rule_carried: For the wage-payment subchapter (342-347): employee unless the employer shows (A) freedom from control, (B) service outside the usual course or places of business, (C) independently established trade (ABC test); employer = any person employing one or more individuals; wages = all remuneration incl. salary, commissions and incentive pay.

instrument_name: 32 V.S.A. 5811(21) Taxable income defined from federal AGI (conformity)
figure_or_rule_carried: Vermont taxable income starts from federal adjusted gross income (without regard to IRC 168(k)), with listed additions (non-VT municipal interest) and subtractions (US obligations, capital-gain exclusion, Social Security/retirement exclusion 5830e, cannabis 280E, student-loan interest), less personal exemption 4,150 per person (statutory base) and standard deduction. No wage-level departure from federal exclusions (401(k), section 125, HSA, transit, group-term life) appears; with GB-1210 (VT withholding follows federal-withholding wages, US-VTS5-016) the VT wage base = federal withholding wages, except civil-union partner benefits treated as spouse benefits.

instrument_name: 12 V.S.A. 3170 Trustee process against earnings: exemptions
figure_or_rule_carried: No trustee-process order against a debtor who received DCF or DVHA assistance in the 2 months before the hearing. Exempt: (1) the greater of 75 pct of weekly disposable earnings or 30x federal minimum hourly wage; (2) consumer-credit judgment debt: the greater of 85 pct of weekly disposable earnings or 40x federal minimum hourly wage (i.e. max 15 pct attachable, stricter than CCPA 25 pct); (3) more if the court finds reasonable expenses exceed these. Order may provide repetitive withholding; 3172 bars discharge for trustee process; waiver void.

instrument_name: 21 V.S.A. 343 Form of payment
figure_or_rule_carried: No payment in scrip, vouchers, due bills or store orders; payment by check (Title 9A) or by electronic fund transfer as in 342 (written authorisation), or by a cooperative corporation to a shareholder-employee (who may demand 342 payment).

instrument_name: 15 V.S.A. 787 Employer's responsibility under child-support wage withholding
figure_or_rule_carried: On notice of wage withholding (Vermont order or similar law of another state): withhold the periodic amount each wage period; forward to the registry within 7 working days of withholding with the withholding date; keep records; stop on notice; notify the registry within 10 days of termination of employment. Employer may retain up to 5.00 USD per month from the obligor for administrative costs. Liability if not started within 10 working days of notice or the next payday (whichever later); late forwarding >30 days: civil penalty up to 100 USD first, 1,000 USD subsequent. Combined remittance allowed with per-employee listing. Withhold only from the non-exempt portion under CCPA 303(b) (15 U.S.C. 1673(b)). Furnish SSN and wages to the Office of Child Support on request.

instrument_name: 21 V.S.A. 345 Nonpayment of wages and benefits (penalties; officer liability)
figure_or_rule_carried: Violation of 342 (pay timing incl. final pay), 343, 482 or 483: fine up to 5,000 USD; corporate officers controlling payment operations liable for wages when willfully participating; failure to pay agreed benefits: actual damages and, if knowing and willful for 30 days, civil penalty up to 5,000 USD.

instrument_name: Vermont DOL WH-13 Summary of Wage and Hour Laws (rev. June 2019): wage deductions, record keeping, vacation/severance
authority: Vermont Department of Labor Wage and Hour Program
figure_or_rule_carried: Deductions (per Minimum Wage Rules): goods/services only if not below minimum wage, with written authorisation or documented intent to repay, not prohibited, not above the agreed amount; deductions authorised by law (taxes, child support); health/retirement contributions with written authorisation; meals and lodging actually furnished and accepted. Commission-only pay is wages with the same deduction protection. Records of hours and wages kept 2 years (21 V.S.A. 393 per the Department; WH-13 says UI law 3 years, but the 06/26 UI handbook says 4 years, US-VTS5-009). No statutory duty to provide holidays, vacation or severance; written agreements/handbooks providing them are enforceable as wages. Rounding of start/finish to 5 min / 0.1 h / 0.25 h accepted if neutral over time. Edition 2019 (predates earned sick time references): mechanics only.

instrument_name: 21 V.S.A. 472 Parental and family leave (unpaid; benefits continue)
figure_or_rule_carried: Up to 12 weeks unpaid leave per 12 months for parental, family, safe leave or a qualifying exigency; up to 2 of the 12 weeks for bereavement (max 5 consecutive workdays); employee may elect to use accrued sick/vacation/other paid leave or short-term disability (does not extend leave); employer continues employment benefits at the same level, may require the existing employee contribution; reinstatement to same or comparable job and pay. Last amendment 2025 No. 32 s. 3 eff. 2025-07-01 (bereavement/safe leave/exigency limbs).

instrument_name: 21 V.S.A. 472a Short-term family leave
figure_or_rule_carried: In addition to 472: unpaid leave up to 4 hours per 30 days and 24 hours per 12 months (employer may require 2-hour minimum segments) for school activities, routine medical/dental appointments, other professional-care appointments or a family medical emergency; notice at least 7 days except emergency; employee may use accrued paid leave at their discretion.

instrument_name: GB-1326 The Vermont Child Care Contribution guide
figure_or_rule_carried: CCC under 32 V.S.A. ch. 246: 0.44 pct of all IRC 3401 wages subject to VT income tax withholding, no wage cap, regardless of hours; employer may withhold up to one-quarter (max 0.11 pct of wages) from employees, may withhold less or none and need not treat all employees alike; employee share reported in W-2 Box 14; employer and employee portions reported on quarterly WHT-436 and paid with withholding; worked split 0.44 = 0.11 employee + 0.33 employer. Self-employed: 0.11 pct of SE income for work physically performed in VT, no cap.
